label: Transaction Bubble
title: Transaction Bubble
summary: Use a Transaction Bubble for one payment in a chat thread: who it was with, the amount, and its status, opening its details.
corePrinciple: One payment per bubble; its details are one tap away.

anatomy.title: Who, how much, and how it went
anatomy.description: The description and the amount sit at the top, anything you pass as children comes next, and the status line and a chevron close the bubble.

configuration.title: Status, a note, your own status line
configuration.description: Set the Transaction Status mode on the bubble to set its status mark: Request an orange “!”, Paid a green tick, Declined a red cross, and Expired, the default, a grey “!”; status and date give the words. children add a row between the amount and the status, such as the note sent with the payment. statusSlot replaces the status line and the chevron with your own content. No other mode changes the bubble.

states.title: A picture, or a button
states.description: Without onPress the bubble is a picture of the payment, but its chevron still shows; if it doesn’t open, drop the chevron with statusSlot. With onPress the whole bubble is one button, and it fades a little while pressed. Its default name is the description and the status word, with no amount or date, so set accessibilityLabel.

Looks the same; the whole bubble presses.

sizing.title: The thread sets the width
sizing.description: The bubble has no width of its own: it fills its host. In Figma’s thread it is 231 px of a 328 px column, on the right for payments you send. With one line of description it is 119 px tall, 10 px taller than Figma’s 109, because the amount sits on a 34 px line. It has 16 px of padding, and its parts are 8 px apart.

content.title: The other person, the amount, one word
content.description: Write description as what happened and with whom, such as Paid to Priya Sharma; it gets one line, so keep it short or set disableTruncation. Give value without a currency sign: currency adds the ₹. Write status as one word that matches the mode, and date short. When the bubble presses, set accessibilityLabel to the person, the amount, the status, and the date.

inContext.title: Payments in a thread
inContext.description: A thread lists the payments between two people: the ones you send sit on the right, the ones you receive on the left. The thread places and sizes the bubbles, 231 px wide here as in Figma, and each bubble’s onPress opens that payment’s details.

sources.title: Use the public Transaction Bubble contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Transaction Bubble exposes one property, Description; its amount and status line are nested instances, and its status comes from the Transaction Status variable mode. The package takes description, value, currency, status, and date as props, and the mode sets the status mark’s icon and colour, as in Figma. The bubble is 119 px tall where Figma’s is 109, its description is Regular where Figma’s is Medium, and its default accessible name leaves out the amount and date. In Storybook, the Successful story keeps the orange mark and the slot story shows two amounts (all reported).
